## Accepted partial results

The exact objective is minimum |S| such that adding the missing clique edges
on S makes a finite simple graph generically globally rigid in the plane.
The general arbitrary-input optimum remains unresolved by this work.

The full analytic proof establishes the sharp delta+1 rigidifying-subset
lemma; an exact n^(delta+O(1)) XP algorithm using the prior constrained
rigid-input optimizer; a sparse redundant-rigidity criterion; equality with
feedback vertex number on simple 3-connected cubic graphs of order at least
twelve; and the exact forest formula. All small-order exceptions, the
zero/one/two additional-vertex completion checks, and separator control are
preserved. The separate appendix proves the all-m disjoint-copy staging
obstruction, with ordinary/global/retained optima (2m,3m,5m) and ratio 5/3
for the displayed allowed first-stage choice.

Király–Mihálykó receive credit for exact rigid-input/constrained completion
and the factor-two arbitrary-input approximation:
https://doi.org/10.1137/21M1432417 . Jordán receives credit for the sparse
rank formula and prior M-connected formulation:
https://egres.elte.hu/tr/egres-09-05.pdf . Ueno–Kajitani–Gotoh receive credit
for polynomial subcubic feedback vertex set:
https://doi.org/10.1016/0012-365X(88)90226-9 .

## Inspection and claim limits

The inspected Király–Mihálykó repository copy is a review manuscript labeled
submitted, not represented as the final publisher PDF. The revised
Mihálykó dissertation retains the required planar theorem for simple rigid
graphs of order at least six; orders at most five are handled directly.
Ueno–Kajitani–Gotoh's primary publisher abstract was inspected, but the full
PDF returned HTTP 403. The cubic polynomial corollary relies on the established
theorem without a new audit of that original full proof.

This AI-assisted, unrefereed edition makes no general resolution, hardness,
FPT, novelty, current-openness, external human peer-review, journal acceptance,
or formal proof-assistant certification claim. The 5/3 obstruction is not a
lower bound for every possible first-stage choice. Aggregate finite checks
supplement complete analytic proofs; no omitted executable is a premise.

## Distribution

Exactly ten authored proof, appendix, audit, acceptance, source-metadata,
status and manifest files are added under
`unsolved_math_prioritization/attempts/3000001/`. Editorial changes preserve
all accepted analytic arguments, remove private workflow/provenance, replace
excluded checker references with qualified aggregate metadata, and bind the
public proof and appendix exactly to their separate acceptances.

Programs, raw generated outputs, datasets, copied third-party source bodies
or images, and private coordination material are excluded. Recorded source
and verification history is not a new retrieval, inspection, literature
search or computation rerun by edition preparation.

QUEUE.md and all unrelated content remain unchanged. The status stays partial
at one of five substantive attempts; editorial preparation adds no proof
turn and resets no historical accounting. No merge, release, DOI, journal
submission or outside outreach is requested.

Base commit: `f6caddda8f8be2cdb3e91494325d8f7f365bc3fc`.
